text.p: Flamengo announced on Wednesday they were abandoning the Rio de Janeiro championship in protest at a decision by the federation to interrupt the competition for a month.
In yet another twist to one of the most bizarre competitions ever held in Brazil, the Rio federation had on Tuesday accepted a request by Vasco da Gama to suspend the competition immediately.
This means that their game against Flamengo on Sunday, which could decide the third stage of the competition, will no longer go ahead.

Vasco made the request because they have two key players with the Brazil national team, which is currently on a European tour and immediately afterwards fly to Bolivia for the Copa America. This could take until June 28 if Brazil reach the final.
The federation did not give any new dates for the remaining matches but said simply they would take place in late June or July.
Flamengo president Kleber Leite launched a vicious personal attack on Vasco vice-president Eurico Miranda, who he blamed for the change in dates, and said his club would abandon the competition.
"We've fitted into the calender they gave us and now they have changed everything," he fumed. "We've gone through the bottom of the hole."
Leite said Flamengo had already arranged to take part in tournaments abroad in July.
Fluminense, who also have a chance to win the third stage, said they could lose half their team by July as many players' contracts finish next month.
The winners of the third stage will face Botafogo, who won the first two stages, in a play-off series in which the first team to reach six points will win the title.
Botafogo will start the series with a four-point advantage by virtue of having won an extra stage.

Vasco, who had goalkeeper Carlos Germano and striker Edmundo included in the Brazil squad, have performed poorly throughout the competition but rekindled their chances of winning the third stage after they beat Botafogo at the weekend.
The championship has been dogged by problems from the start.
Botafogo, Fluminense and Flamengo boycotted the opening weekend in protest at the format. It was subsequently modified.

One match started nearly one hour late because the two teams argued over the colour of their shorts while in another game a coach ran on to his pitch and dropped his trousers in a protest over the refereeing.
Flamengo striker Romario escaped suspension through "lack of evidence" after becoming involved in a punch-up with a Madureira opponent. The fight was seen by millions on television.

A second meeting between Flamengo and Madureira was held up for 15 minutes by a brawl which started with Madureira players attacking a linesman -- one of three matches to be interrupted by fights requiring intervention by armed police.

In another match, Vasco fans chanted "it's a fix" and "robbery" after seeing their team score in the fourth and sixth minutes of injury time to win 2-1 against a Volta Redonda team down to nine men after two players had been sent off.
